messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Can RHIPE process SequenceFiles of arbitrary key/value types, such as Text or BytesWritable?  or does it only support keys and values of type RHBytesWritable?

(In short: I have created a SequenceFile with key type=Text, value type=BytesWritable.  When I try to work with this data using RHIPE my Map expression doesn't see the keys and values as expected: map.keys is just a set of numbers and map.values appears to be raw chunks of the input SequenceFile.)

Thanks.

Maybe one should write an Inputformat that uses protocol buffer objects. Like Sequence Files.

messages.subject_clean: Avro bindings for RHIPE?
messages.body_plain:
I am building java+scala bridges to R that have a lot in common with
the RHIPE reqts.
I will definitely use RHIPE as soon as I have access to a HadoopFS
setup!
Until then (and even after then when I'm in "local experiment" mode),
I would like to
use Java mappings that are as compatible with RHIPE as possible (so R
+Java
experiments will run "the same way", semantically, using local JVM vs.
Hadoop cloud).

In Saptarshi's presentation of 2010-08-13, on Todo slide 24, he asks,
"Move to Avro serialization?"    I wouldn't want anyone to have to
"move",
necessarily, but it would be very nice to have Avro-Java bindings for
R!

Do others in the R + Hadoop community see large potential benefit in
having
Avro available as a channel (in addition to protobuf, at least at
first)?
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Why I care, in case you care:

We have committed to using Avro as the serialization format for the
following projects,
which will all benefit from connectivity to R (as well as Hadoop):

   www.appdapter.org <http://www.appdapter.org>,   www.cogchar.org <http://www.cogchar.org>,    www.robokind.org <http://www.robokind.org>   <-
Apache license.
   www.bucksum.com <http://www.bucksum.com> <- financial, closed source for now.

We have Avro serialization working over QPid, but have not tried it
yet with Hadoop.
We chose Avro in part because we like the design, in part because we
have expected
Avro to become the best way to serialize for Hadoop.  I recognize that
not all of Hadoop
has been bound to Avro yet, but I am not current on the details;  I
assume Avro
is still the long term strategic direction.  True?

We could contribute to an effort to make RHIPE more Avro friendly, if
others are interested.

peace,

Stu

messages.subject_clean: Running R/Rhipe Mapreduce jobs on Amazon elastic MapReduce
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

We, in our project, are exploring the option of running mapreduce jobs
using Amazon elastic MapReduce on AWS. We already have these jobs
coded in R using Rhipe.But unfortunately couldn't find much help on
the  Amazon elastic MapReduce page regarding jobs in R and Rhipe. Of
course I saw we can submit R jobs using Hadoop streaming work flow for
which we will need to have the mapper and reducer as seperate .R files
and that too completely coded in R.

The main problem I believe we will be facing in regards to running our
MR jobs on  Amazon is that Rhipe (and R if it is not provided) will
have to be installed on cloud on all the instances(But the resource
allocation itself is dynamic,i.e.,we get a new instance every time and
hence would have to install Rhipe and its requisites every time).
Porting the entire MR from R to say Pig which is supported more on
Amazon elastic MapReduce would be very cumbersome and would prefer to
avoid that.
